dimensions.justification: Specific problem with volume, effort and wait figures from the extraction (M-1, M-2, M-7), stated apart from the LLM solution; no alternative hypotheses.

The case rests on figures stated in the meeting (M-1 to M-7): no provider data, no evidence cards, no anecdote records and no confidence levels per figure. 6c lists the gaps and how to close them, but evidence that was only spoken is a claim, so this is a 2.
dimensions.fix: Close the gaps in 6c: configure a data provider and an anecdote source, re-run the figures through them, and attach a confidence level to each figure.

dimensions.justification: Cost savings and faster fulfilment are stated and cited (M-3, S-2); the notes give no deadline or wider strategy and the PRD says so.
One primary metric (MET-001) with the 80% target from the notes (M-6), a known baseline of fully manual parsing, three guardrails and instrumentation.
Non-goals in section 7 and in/out lists in section 13, anchored on human review of every parse (R-1).
Data readiness (M-4), the 4 week MVP estimate (M-8) and open data-quality and cost questions are listed as dependencies and open questions.
All eight requirements have Given/When/Then criteria, including a fallback and an unparseable-input case.
Misparse, drift, sparse types, rubber-stamping and unverified evidence each carry a mitigation.
Claims cite extraction IDs, REQ and MET IDs are numbered, numbers in sections 2, 3 and 6 trace to the extraction, and the decision log states that the extraction has no decision items.
A1 restates the five gates with citations, notes the data-quality caveat on gate 3 and finds no red flags; alternatives to a fine-tuned model are only briefly compared.
A5 to A7 give confidence flags, full reviewer control, a manual fallback and explicit never-do constraints.
A8 has four weighted dimensions on a 1 to 4 scale, must-pass thresholds, and a golden set of good, bad, edge and failure cases with a 50 or more target; weights are marked as proposals.
